title: Explode array in json in Pyspark
question:
I want to extract the json and array from it in a efficient way to avoid using lambda. I also had used array_zip but the array size in col_1, col_2 and col_3 are not same. Thanks in advance. I have a data like this

data = [
    Row(
        id="1",
        json_data=(
            """{
            "col_1": [{"date": {"time": "2012-10-09T16:54:32+00:00"}, "value": -0.03},
                      {"date": {"time": "2012-10-09T16:54:33+00:00"}, "value": -1.03}],
            "col_2": [{"date": {"time": "2012-10-09T16:54:32+00:00"}, "value": 0.06},
               {"date": {"time": "2012-10-09T16:54:33+00:00"}, "value": 1.06},
               {"date": {"time": "2012-10-09T16:54:34+00:00"}, "value": -0.02}],
            "col_3": [{"date": {"time": "2012-10-09T16:54:31+00:00"}, "value": 10},
               {"date": {"time": "2012-10-09T16:54:32+00:00"}, "value": 7},
            {"date": {"time": "2012-10-09T16:54:33+00:00"}, "value": 8.43}],
            }"""
        )
    )
]

and expecting output like this

+--+------------------------+------+------+-----+
|id|time                    |col_1 |col_2 |col_3|
+--+------------------------+------+------+-----+
|1|2012-10-09T16:54:31+00:00|null  |null  |10.0 |
|1|2012-10-09T16:54:32+00:00|-0.03 |0.06  |7.0  |
|1|2012-10-09T16:54:33+00:00|-1.03 |1.06  |8.43 |
|1|2012-10-09T16:54:34+00:00|null  |-0.02 |null |
+--+------------------------+------+------+-----+

I tried with below code, but I have a large data and I want to make more efficient code, Is there any another way of doing this than lambda?

json_schema = StructType([
    StructField("col_1", ArrayType(StructType([
        StructField("date", StructType([
            StructField("time", StringType())
        ])),
        StructField("value", DoubleType())
    ]))),
    StructField("col_2", ArrayType(StructType([
        StructField("date", StructType([
            StructField("time", StringType())
        ])),
        StructField("value", DoubleType())
    ]))),
    StructField("col_3", ArrayType(StructType([
        StructField("date", StructType([
            StructField("time", StringType())
        ])),
        StructField("value", DoubleType())
    ])))
])


parsed_df = df.withColumn("parsed", F.from_json(df.data, json_schema))
    
timestamps_df = parsed_df.select(
    parsed_df.id,
    F.explode(
        F.array_distinct(
            F.concat(
                F.transform("parsed.col_1", lambda x: x.date.time),
                F.transform("parsed.col_2", lambda x: x.date.time),
                F.transform("parsed.col_3", lambda x: x.date.time)
            )
        )
    ).alias("time")
)

def find_value_for_time(array_col, time_col):
    return F.expr(f"""
        CASE 
            WHEN size(filter({array_col}, x -> x.date.time = {time_col})) > 0
            THEN (filter({array_col}, x -> x.date.time = {time_col}))[0].value
            ELSE NULL
        END
    """)

result = timestamps_df.join(parsed_df, "id").select(
    "id",
    "time",
    find_value_for_time("parsed.col_1", "time").alias("col_1"),
    find_value_for_time("parsed.col_2", "time").alias("col_2"),
    find_value_for_time("parsed.col_3", "time").alias("col_3")
)

result = result.orderBy("time")
answer:
I don't know whether your data is large in what way whether you have more "col_x" or you have more data within the array, so not sure if this is more performant or not but here is the alternative code you can try.

Also, I don't think lambda is the bottleneck in your code. orderBy is one of the slowest part as this is an intensive operation. If you don't have to sort it in Pyspark, try removing it. Then, join can be slow when tables to be joined are large.

Anyhow, here is my code to achieve the same result.

cols = ['col_1', 'col_2', 'col_3']
df = (df.select('id', 'parsed.*') # Breakdown 1.
      .select('id', *[F.transform(c, lambda x: F.struct(x.date.time, F.lit(c).alias('ori_col_name'), x.value)).alias(c)
                      for c in cols]) # 2.
      .select('id', F.explode(F.concat(*[c for c in cols]).alias('col'))) # 3.
      .select('id', 'col.*') # 4.
      .groupby('id', 'time') # 5.
      .pivot('ori_col_name') # 5.
      .agg(F.max('value'))) # 5.

Breakdown

  1. Use select with * to flatten the struct.
  2. Use transform to extract time, value, and add the key name as a value in struct. This allows me to align on the struct column names. After this line, the schema should look like
root
 |-- id: string (nullable = true)
 |-- col_1: array (nullable = true)
 |    |-- element: struct (containsNull = false)
 |    |    |-- time: string (nullable = true)
 |    |    |-- ori_col_name: string (nullable = false)
 |    |    |-- value: double (nullable = true)
 |-- col_2: array (nullable = true)
 |    |-- element: struct (containsNull = false)
 |    |    |-- time: string (nullable = true)
 |    |    |-- ori_col_name: string (nullable = false)
 |    |    |-- value: double (nullable = true)
 |-- col_3: array (nullable = true)
 |    |-- element: struct (containsNull = false)
 |    |    |-- time: string (nullable = true)
 |    |    |-- ori_col_name: string (nullable = false)
 |    |    |-- value: double (nullable = true)
  1. Concat all col_1, col_2, col_3 into a single array then explode it once.
  2. Flatten the exploded array. After this, the dataframe should look like this.
+---+-------------------------+------------+-----+
|id |time                     |ori_col_name|value|
+---+-------------------------+------------+-----+
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:32+00:00|col_1       |-0.03|
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:33+00:00|col_1       |-1.03|
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:32+00:00|col_2       |0.06 |
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:33+00:00|col_2       |1.06 |
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:34+00:00|col_2       |-0.02|
+---+-------------------------+------------+-----+
  1. Then we can pivot this dataframe to achieve your desired output.

Result

+---+-------------------------+-----+-----+-----+
|id |time                     |col_1|col_2|col_3|
+---+-------------------------+-----+-----+-----+
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:33+00:00|-1.03|1.06 |8.43 |
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:34+00:00|NULL |-0.02|NULL |
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:32+00:00|-0.03|0.06 |7.0  |
|1  |2012-10-09T16:54:31+00:00|NULL |NULL |10.0 |
+---+-------------------------+-----+-----+-----+
